subject: Dedicated inference scope and burst alignment - recap
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Sara Kline <sara.kline@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Dedicated inference scope and burst alignment - recap

Sara — thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our call so we have an agreed starting point and clear next steps. I captured what I heard; please correct anything I missed.

Key pain points
- Production variability: monthly batch jobs + marketing spikes cause 6x traffic variance; current provider throttles during peaks.
- Security/isolation: PHI scope means Veridian requires tenant isolation and audit logs (SOC2 + HIPAA addendum likely).
- Cost unpredictability: token costs spike during bursts; need predictable committed unit economics.

Goals and success criteria
- Baseline throughput: sustained 150 qps for model A (short-form summarization) and burst to 900 qps for up to 6 hours during month-end windows.
- Latency SLO: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 120ms, p99 target ~200ms for typical sequences (we discussed shorter/longer models separately).
- Isolation: dedicated GPU pool per environment (prod only initially), with audit logs retained 365 days.
- Onboarding timeline: pilot in Q3 (target start 2027-07-01), production ramp over 8–12 weeks after successful pilot.

Our immediate recommendations (what we’ll do next)
1) Draft SLA + pricing sketch (attached: redwood-dedicated-sla-draft.pdf) — Evelyn to send initial commercial and SLA language by EOD.
2) Technical deep-dive — schedule a 60‑min session next week with Ben to map throughput profile and model footprints. Please share model names + average and 95th pct sequence lengths ahead of that call.
3) Ops/runbook alignment — we’ll provide an ops runbook template and request your on-call rotation and escalation contacts.
4) Procurement path — we’ll include standard PO and HIPAA addendum templates for your procurement team.

Open questions for Veridian
- Can you share a 7‑day request trace (JSON or CSV) showing peak-minute qps and token distributions?
- Any hard constraints on regionalization (need all traffic kept in us‑east only)?
- Which models are latency-sensitive vs throughput-sensitive (we can propose quantization/packing tradeoffs per model).

Next steps (proposed)
- Sara: confirm available times for the deep-dive (Ben + Jasmine + Evelyn).
- Veridian procurement: we’ll send the SLA + HIPAA addendum for initial review.
- Ben: prepare a quick ops/architecture note on burst isolation and warm-up strategies.

Thanks again — looking forward to aligning on the pilot.

—
Evelyn Hart
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192
Redwood Inference
From: Sara Kline <sara.kline@veridianhealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:23:14 -04:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated inference scope and burst alignment - recap

Thanks, Evelyn — this is exactly the kind of crisp recap we needed. A few clarifications from our side:

Confirmations
- Baseline and burst: the 150 qps baseline and 900 qps burst look right for our prod summarization traffic. Bursts are concentrated to a 4–8 hour window at month-end but can happen other times with smaller magnitude.
- Isolation: prod must be logically and physically isolated from other Veridian tenants; we’re fine if Redwood provides a dedicated pool per Veridian (not per-tenant).

Procurement notes
- Procurement would like an estimated monthly committed spend for the pilot (so they can provision a PO). Could you provide a ballpark committed-dollar figure for the proposed pilot size and a separate estimate for steady-state after ramp?
- HIPAA and data residency: must remain within us regions — happy to sign Redwood's HIPAA addendum once we review.

Scheduling
- Deep-dive: Thu 22 Apr 2027 between 09:00–11:00 EDT works for me. I’ll invite our infra lead (cc procurement if there are commercial questions).

We will assemble a short trace and share by EOD Wed. Thanks again — Sara

—
Sara Kline
Head of AI Platforms, Veridian Health
sara.kline@veridianhealth.com | +1 212-555-0147

Perfect — Thu 22 Apr 09:30 EDT booked on our side; invite received.

Commercials: we’ll send a conservative pilot pricing sketch in the SLA draft tonight; high level ballpark ranges so procurement can size a PO:
- Pilot (8 weeks, isolated prod pool): $55k–$85k committed estimate (depends on final burst window tolerance and ops retention).
- Steady-state (after ramp to production): $18k–$30k/month for the baseline pool + burst buffer pricing on an as‑used basis or pre-committed burst credits.

What Ben/Jasmine need before the deep-dive
- Model names + container images (or HF model ids).
- Typical and 95th percentile sequence lengths per model.
- Peak per-minute qps and a sample 7‑day trace if possible (you said you’d share tomorrow).

I attached the SLA draft (redwood-dedicated-sla-draft.pdf) for procurement's initial read. We’ll include HIPAA addendum language and data residency commitments in the next revision.

See you Thu.

—
Evelyn
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sara Kline <sara.kline@veridianhealth.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated inference scope and burst alignment - recap

Sara, quick technical note ahead of Thu:

1) Burst mechanics and warm-up
- For a sustained 900 qps burst we recommend pre-warmed standby capacity for the first 30–60 minutes. Without warm standby, cold-start to full throughput can add 10–30% latency and transient queuing.

2) Isolation approach
- We’ll map Veridian to a dedicated GPU pool with tenant-level network ACLs and KMS-backed keys. Audit logs and request tracing will be shipped to your SIEM or retained in Redwood with the retention window you specify.

3) Cost/packing levers we’ll evaluate in the deep-dive
- Quantization profile per model (8-bit / 4-bit), batching targets (batch sizes 8–32 depending on seq length), and KV cache reuse across requests. These moves can materially reduce cost during baseline while preserving burst headroom.

4) What we need from you (technical)
- Model ids + typical seq len (as Evelyn requested).
- If models use tool-calling or external data fetches, flag them — those patterns increase tail latencies and we’ll design fallbacks.

I attached a lightweight ops/runbook template (veridian-ops-runbook-template.xlsx) with warm-up, monitoring, and escalation sections — we can walk it through on Thu.

Looking forward to the deep-dive.

—
Ben Carter
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
